title: Watch: House Democrats Storm Speaker Johnson's Office | TRUTH Press
text:
Democratic lawmakers stormed House Speaker Mike Johnson’s office Tuesday night, demanding he immediately swear in Arizona Rep.-elect Adelita Grijalva.
Johnson was not in his office when the confrontation unfolded.
‘Swear Her In!’
Rep. Pramila Jayapal led the march alongside Reps. Melanie Stansbury and Nanette Barragán.
They joined Grijalva and members of the Democratic Women’s Caucus, chanting “Swear her in!” as they marched through the Capitol.
Capitol Police officers blocked the group from entering Johnson’s office.
Video showed Jayapal and Stansbury tampering with the sign outside the Speaker’s door during the confrontation.
BREAKING 🚨 House Democrats are STORMING Speaker Mike Johnson’s office. They look foolish
LMAO Democrats are so unhinged
Looks like an insurrection
[pic.twitter.com/v1fxCo8elw]— MAGA Voice (@MAGAVoice)
[October 15, 2025]
Footage from multiple angles showed Barragán arguing with an officer who tried to stop her.
Grijalva’s Statement
Grijalva posted a video on X standing outside the Speaker’s office.
“Hi, friends. Adelita Grijalva, your congresswoman-elect,” she said.
“I was certified today. That means the governor, the attorney general, and the secretary of state have all said yes, she won.”
.
[@SpeakerJohnson]You ready to swear me in?[pic.twitter.com/9FHRYUT7RD]— Adelita Grijalva (@AdelitaForAZ)
[October 15, 2025]
“Now they’re asking Speaker Johnson to swear me in,” she continued.
Grijalva said she would remain in Washington “for two days” until Johnson agreed to swear her in.
In a written statement, Grijalva said she won her election “decisively by more than 40,000 votes.”
She thanked Governor Katie Hobbs, Attorney General Kris Mayes, and Secretary Adrian Fontes for certifying the result.
“They did their jobs,” Grijalva wrote. “Now it’s time for Speaker Johnson to do his.”
Grijalva accused Johnson of stalling because she would become “the 218th signature on the discharge petition to release the Epstein files.”
She said his delay was “silencing over 800,000 Southern Arizonans” who currently lack representation during the government shutdown.
Johnson Responds
Speaker Johnson brushed off the protest as a “political stunt.”
“They stormed my office,” Johnson said Wednesday. “They berated a Capitol Police officer, screamed at him. He was just standing at his post.”
He said the incident showed Democrats’ “disdain for law enforcement.”
Johnson added that lawmakers entered his foyer and “tore down a sign” before leaving.
“It shows their desperation,” he said.
Democrat Defense
Rep. Teresa Leger Fernández, chair of the Democratic Women’s Caucus, defended the protest as peaceful.
“Is Speaker Johnson saying Members can no longer walk in the halls of the people’s House to express our viewpoints?” she asked.
A caucus spokesperson denied that members tore down the sign, claiming Barragán simply placed it on the ground.
Barragán said the officer “grabbed me by the side” because he didn’t realize she was a member of Congress.
She said she plans to report the incident to the Capitol Police supervisor.
Republican Reaction
House Majority Whip Tom Emmer criticized the protest as “childish political theater.”
“Democrats can gallivant around the Capitol making ridiculous videos and screaming at police officers who aren’t getting paid,” Emmer said.
He accused Democrats of trying to distract from their “hate America rally” planned for the weekend.
Legal Pressure
Arizona Attorney General Kris Mayes has threatened legal action if Johnson fails to confirm when Grijalva will be sworn in.
Democrats vowed to continue pressuring the Speaker until she takes her oath.
By late Tuesday, Capitol Police had cleared the hallway outside Johnson’s office as tensions on the Hill continued to rise.
